[[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] state assemblyman [[Zohran Mamdani]] won the election with 50.78% of the vote, defeating [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] activist [[Curtis Sliwa]] and [[Independent politician|independent]] former Democratic governor [[Andrew Cuomo]].{{Cite web |last1=Clark |first1=Nell |last2=Yee |first2=Curtis |last3=Mcghee |first3=Bernard |last4=Price |first4=Michelle L. |last5=Vileira |first5=Luena Rodriguez-Feo |last6=Thomas |first6=Ashley |last7=Doyle |first7=Kiana |title=Election Night Live updates: Democrat Zohran Mamdani is elected New York City mayor |url=https://apnews.com/live/2025-election-updates-news |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=AP News |language=en}}{{cite news |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/mamdani-wins-nyc-mayoral-election-2025/ |title=Zohran Mamdani wins NYC mayoral election after energizing young voters with focus on affordability |publisher=[[CBS News]] |access-date=November 4, 2025}}{{Cite web |url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/2025-elections/new-york-city-mayor-results |title=New York City Mayor Results 2025 |access-date=November 4, 2025 |website=NBC News}} This election featured the highest turnout for a New York City mayoral election since [[1993 New York City mayoral election|1993]], mainly due to significant young voter registration.{{Cite web |last1=Bergin |first1=Brigid |last2=HongShare |first2=Joe |date=November 3, 2025 |title=NYC mayor's race gets record early turnout fueled by young voters |url=https://gothamist.com/news/nyc-mayors-race-gets-record-early-turnout-fueled-by-young-voters |website=Gothamist}}{{Cite news |date=2025-11-04 |title=NYC Mayoral Election Live Updates: Mamdani Wins After Highest Turnout in Decades |url=https://www.nytimes.com/live/2025/11/04/nyregion/nyc-mayor-election |access-date=2025-11-05 |language=en}} Mamdani succeeded Democratic incumbent [[Eric Adams]] on January 1, 2026, becoming the first [[Muslims|Muslim]] and first South Asian mayor of New York City, as well as its youngest since [[Hugh J. Grant]] in 1892.{{Cite web |last=Zurcher |first=Anthony |date=2025-11-05 |title=Mamdani seals remarkable victory - but real challenges await |url=https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cly4kr8gzr2o |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=BBC News |language=en-gb}} Adams initially ran for a second term (at first as a Democrat, and later as an independent), but withdrew from the race in September 2025. He remained on the voting ballot because he ended his campaign too late for his name to be removed. Cuomo, pursuing a political comeback after he [[Resignation of Andrew Cuomo|resigned as New York governor in 2021]], was the frontrunner for the Democratic nomination as of early June 2025; however, he was defeated by Mamdani in [[2025 New York City Democratic mayoral primary|the Democratic primary]] in a major [[Upset (politics)|upset]].{{Cite news |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/zohran-mamdani-wins-democratic-nomination-nyc-mayor/ |title=Zohran Mamdani clinches Democratic nomination for NYC mayor |last1=Prussin |first1=Mark |last2=Kramer |first2=Marcia |work=[[CBS News]] |date=July 1, 2025 |access-date=July 1, 2025}} Following his primary loss, Cuomo launched an independent campaign. Sliwa, the Republican nominee in the [[2021 New York City mayoral election]], ran unopposed for his party's nomination. Mamdani ran on a [[democratic socialist]] platform focusing on [[affordability]]. Cuomo ran on a broadly [[centrist]] platform with a focus on crime and combating [[antisemitism]] while also being endorsed by [[Donald Trump]], an endorsement Cuomo declined,{{Cite web |date=2025-11-03 |title=NYC Mayor's Race: Cuomo rejects Trump's apparent endorsement, says he 'called me a bad Democrat' – amNewYork |url=https://www.amny.com/politics/cuomo-rejects-trump-mayors-race/ |access-date=2025-12-12 |website=www.amny.com |language=en-US}}{{Cite web |last=Strauss |first=Joseph |date=2025-10-31 |title=The JTA Q&A with Andrew Cuomo: Antisemitism is a 'deeply personal' fight |url=https://www.jta.org/2025/10/31/united-states/the-jta-qa-with-andrew-cuomo-antisemitism-is-a-deeply-personal-fight |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=Jewish Telegraphic Agency |language=en-US}}{{cite web |title=Eric Adams, Andrew Cuomo focus on crime as race for New York City mayor heats up |url=https://abc7ny.com/post/nyc-mayoral-race-eric-adams-andrew-cuomo-focus-crime-biggest-issues-facing-candidates/16003755/ |website=[[WABC-TV|ABC7 New York]] |date=March 10, 2025 |access-date=November 5, 2025}}{{Cite web|url=https://fortune.com/2025/10/24/eric-adams-endorses-andrew-cuomo-for-mayor-zohran-mamdani/|title=Cuomo used to be a 'snake and a liar' to Eric Adams. Now he's a 'brother' in the fight against Zohran Mamdani|last1=Izaguirre|first1=Anthony|last2=Offenhartz|first2=Jake|agency=Associated Press|website=Fortune|date=2025-10-24}} while Sliwa criticized both from the [[political right]] and advocated [[tough on crime]] policies.{{Cite web |last=Shivonne |first=Adeja |date=2025-11-03 |title=Everything to know about Curtis Sliwa: Platform, experience, background |url=https://www.fox5ny.com/news/curtis-sliwa-election-day-profile |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=FOX 5 NY |language=en-US}}{{Cite web|url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/11/04/politics/nyc-mayor-race-zohran-mamdani-catchup|title=Cuomo, Mamdani, Sliwa: What to know ahead of the NYC mayoral election | CNN Politics|date=November 4, 2025|website=CNN}} Mamdani became the first mayoral candidate since [[1969 New York City mayoral election|1969]] to receive more than one million votes,{{Cite news |last1=Fandos |first1=Nicholas |last2=Jeffery C. |first2=Mays |date=2025-11-05 |title=Takeaways From the NYC Mayoral Election and Zohran Mamdani's Stunning Win |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/05/nyregion/nyc-mayor-election-mamdani-takeaways.html |access-date=2025-11-05 |work=The New York Times |language=en |quote=He was the first candidate since John V. Lindsay in 1969 to win over one million votes in a mayoral election in the five boroughs.}} and the race was the first since 1969 to attract more than two million votes in total.{{Cite web |date=November 4, 2025|title= Voter Turnout Highest in Half Century as Mamdani Phenomenon Galvanizes Electorate|url=https://www.thecity.nyc/2025/11/04/record-voters-ballots-cast-mamdani-cuomo-sliwa/|access-date=November 6, 2025 |website=[[The City (website)|The City]] |language=en}} == Background == [[Eric Adams]] was elected [[mayor of New York City]] in the [[2021 New York City mayoral election|2021 mayoral election]], narrowly winning [[2021 New York City Democratic mayoral primary|the Democratic primary election]] and defeating the Republican nominee, [[Curtis Sliwa]], in the general election in a [[landslide victory]]. In September 2024, a [[Investigations into the Eric Adams administration|series of investigations into the Adams administration]] emerged. Adams was indicted on federal charges of bribery, fraud, and soliciting illegal foreign campaign donations.{{Cite web |last1=Rashbaum |first1=William |last2=Rubinstein |first2=Dana |last3=Rothfeld |first3=Michael |last4=Haag |first4=Matthew |date=September 25, 2024 |title=Eric Adams Is Indicted in New York |url=https://www.nytimes.com/live/2024/09/25/nyregion/eric-adams-indicted-corruption |url-access=registration |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240926010831/https://www.nytimes.com/live/2024/09/25/nyregion/eric-adams-indicted-corruption |archive-date=September 26, 2024 |access-date=September 25, 2024 |work=[[The New York Times]]}} Adams pleaded not guilty to the charges. Adams was the first New York City mayor to be charged with crimes while in office, and he received several calls to resign before the end of his term.{{Cite news |last1=Honan |first1=Katie following the announcement of his intention to run.{{Cite web|url=https://abc7ny.com/post/former-governor-andrew-cuomo-leads-new-york-city-mayoral-election-polls-eric-adams-falls-behind-zohran-mamdani/16090506/|title=Andrew Cuomo leads in New York City for mayor.{{cite news |last=Rubinstein |first=Dana |date=July 1, 2025 |title=Zohran Mamdani Wins N.Y.C. Mayoral Primary in Decisive 12-Point Victory |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/07/01/nyregion/mamdani-wins-mayor-primary-nyc.html |url-access=registration |newspaper=The New York Times}} Mamdani's victory was considered a major upset.{{cite web|author1=Adler, Ben|author2=Powel, James|author3=Cuevas, Eduardo|author4=Kuafman, Anna|author5=Kochi, Sudiksha |date=June 25, 2025|title=Recap: Zohran Mamdani pulls off NYC Democratic mayoral upset. Andrew Cuomo concedes |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/politics/2025/06/24/nyc-mayoral-democratic-primary-cuomo-mamdani/84292986007/ |website=USA Today |access-date=June 25, 2025}} Mamdani suggested imposing a flat 2% tax on New Yorkers who earn more than $1 million and a number of housing plans, such as a promise to freeze rents on rent-stabilized units, extensive public housing development and refurbishment, and stricter regulation of landlords, upsetting some in the luxury real estate market.{{cite web | last1=Delouya | first1=Samantha | last2=Buchwald | first2=Elisabeth | title=Mamdani win sends jitters through NYC luxury real estate market | website=CNN | date=July 14, 2025 | url=https://edition.cnn.com/2025/07/14/business/zohran-mamdani-new-york-real-estate-florida | access-date=July 15, 2025}} Nevertheless, Cuomo, who also filed to run on the independent "Fight and Deliver" ballot line,{{cite news|url=https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/politics/2025/05/07/andrew-cuomo-mayor-independent-candidate-|title=Cuomo to also run as independent for mayor|first=Erica|last=Brosnan|publisher=Spectrum News|date=May 7, 2025|access-date=June 26, 2025}}{{cite news|url=https://abc3340.com/news/nation-world/former-governor-andrew-cuomo-plans-independent-run-for-new-york-city-mayoral-race|title=Former Gov. Walden sued to challenge a law that bans the use of the words "independent" and "independence" in political party names. in New York City Mayoral Race |date=September 8, 2025 |access-date=September 8, 2025 |website=Independent Political Report}} ==Campaign== ===Campaign trail=== [[File:Zohran Mamdani at the Resist Fascism Rally in Bryant Park on Oct 27th 2024.jpg|thumb|Mamdani in October 2024]] After Zohran Mamdani won the Democratic primary in June 2025, several business executives reportedly began meeting with incumbent Eric Adams as they considered backing him in the general election.{{cite news |last1=Rosman |first1=Katherine |last2=Rubenstein |first2=Dana |date=June 25, 2025 |title=Eric Adams Meets With Business Leaders Desperate to Stop Mamdani's Rise |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/06/26/nyregion/eric-adams-business-leaders-meeting.html |url-access=registration |access-date=June 27, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]]}} Jim Walden called for all "non-Mamdani" candidates to "coalesce" around one candidate in the weeks just before the election, in order to prevent [[spoiler effect|vote splitting]]. Several Republicans in the weeks afterward pressured Curtis Sliwa to drop out in order to shore up support for Adams, but Sliwa repeated on July 7 that he would not.{{Cite web |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/07/07/nyc-mayor-adams-says-cuomo-pushing-him-to-drop-out-of-race-to-maximize-chances-against-mamdani/ |title=NYC Mayor Adams says Cuomo pushing him to drop out of race to maximize chances against Mamdani |first1=Chris |last1=Sommerfeldt |first2=Josephine |last2=Stratman |work=[[New York Daily News]] |date=July 7, 2025 |access-date=July 12, 2025}} Walden later doubled down, pledging to drop out of the race by September if he was not the leading "non-Mamdani" candidate while giving an interview to [[CBS News]] on ''The Point''.{{cite web |last=Anderson |first=Renee |title=Jim Walden, independent candidate for NYC mayor, backs pledge to drop out if not leading by September |url=https://www.cbsnews.com/newyork/news/jim-walden-nyc-mayor-election-independent-candidates/ |website=[[CBS News]] |date=July 20, 2025 |access-date=August 8, 2025}} Walden would drop out of the race on September 2, again urging for a "one-on-one race" and calling Mamdani the "most dangerous" option for mayor.{{cite web |last1=Rubinstein |first1=Dana |last2=Fandos |first2=Nicholas |date=September 2, 2025 |title=Jim Walden Suspends Campaign for Mayor of New York City |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/02/nyregion/jim-walden-mayor-campaign.html |url-access=registration |access-date=September 7, 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]]}} On July 1, President [[Donald Trump]] voiced support for Adams, describing him as a "very good person" and stating that he "helped him out a little bit"—in reference to his corruption case being dropped by Trump's Department of Justice—while also threatening to arrest Mamdani.{{Cite web |last=Benen |first=Steve |date=2025-07-02 |title=On Eric Adams' corruption case, Trump says 'a little bit' more than he should have |url=https://www.msnbc.com/rachel-maddow-show/maddowblog/eric-adams-corruption-case-trump-says-little-bit-rcna216479 |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=[[MSNBC]] |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Benen |first=Steve |date=2025-07-02 |title=Trump intensifies offensive against NYC's Zohran Mamdani, muses about possible 'arrest' |url=https://www.msnbc.com/rachel-maddow-show/maddowblog/trump-intensifies-offensive-nycs-zohran-mamdani-muses-possible-arrest-rcna216462 |access-date=2025-11-05 |website=[[MSNBC]] |language=en}} During an unrelated press conference, Adams commented that "anyone that is an elected or not should never interfere with federal authorities carrying out their functions".{{cite web |last1=Donaldson |first1=Sahalie |title=Trump voices support for Eric Adams, threatens Zohran Mamdani |url=https://www.cityandstateny.com/politics/2025/07/trump-voices-support-eric-adams-threatens-zohran-mamdani/406458/?oref=csny-skybox-hp |website=[[City & State]] |date=July 2025 |access-date=July 12, 2025}} Trump also suggested the possibility of placing New York under federal control if Mamdani wins. In September 2025, ''[[The New York Times]]'' began reporting that Adams had allegedly met in Florida with [[Steve Witkoff]], an advisor to Trump, about receiving a position in the president's administration, specifically as an [[Ambassadors of the United States|ambassador]], in return for him dropping out and increasing the chances of Mamdani being defeated. Later reports suggested that Adams was giving serious consideration to the proposition despite public statements denying it; part of this consideration was whether or not he would have to resign from his position as mayor.{{Cite news |date=September 3, 2025 |title=Trump Advisers Have Discussed a Job for Adams if He Quits Mayor's Race |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/03/nyregion/trump-adams-sliwa-quit-nyc-mayor.html |access-date=September 5, 2025 |language=en}}{{Cite news |date=September 4, 2025 |title=Adams Considers Dropping Out of Race After Secret Meeting in Florida |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/09/04/nyregion/adams-trump-job-quits.html |access-date=September 5, 2025 |language=en}} Adams initially responded with a statement on September 5 that he would not be withdrawing from the race.{{Cite web |date=September 5, 2025 |title=NYC Mayor Eric Adams insists he's sticking with his reelection bid |url=https://apnews.com/article/eric-adams-trump-job-offer-nyc-mayor-1005e2938a564324fe07206fc16dc164 |access-date=September 5, 2025 |website=AP News |language=en}} Adams later withdrew his candidacy on September 28,{{Cite web |last=Pazmino |first=Gloria |date=September 28, 2025 |title=New York City Mayor Eric Adams suspends his reelection bid |url=https://www.cnn.com/2025/09/28/politics/new-york-city-mayor-eric-adams-suspends-his-reelection-bid |access-date=September 28, 2025 |website=CNN |language=en}} stating that his campaign was "underserved, the marginalized, the abandoned and betrayed by government" as both the state and national Democratic parties increasingly coalesced around Mamdani instead of Adams. Republican candidate Curtis Sliwa, in response to Trump's comments regarding the race, portrayed himself as an [[anti-Trump Republican]], saying that "[Trump] should stay out of [New York politics]", while running a [[grassroots politics|grassroots]] campaign.{{cite web |last1=Harry |first1=Ayana |title=Curtis Sliwa focuses on grassroots campaign as race for mayor intensifies |url=https://ny1.com/nyc/all-boroughs/politics/2025/07/21/curtis-sliwa-focuses-on-grassroots-campaign-as-race-for-mayor-intensifies |website=[[NY1]] |access-date=July 25, 2025}} By early August, Sliwa began reworking his own personal style and his platform, foregoing his iconic red beret, claiming it had become too much of a "defining issue" distracting from his campaign.{{cite web |last1=Fandos |first1=Nicholas |date=August 3, 2025 |title=Curtis Sliwa Wants to Be Mayor. He's Taking Off His Beret to Prove It. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/03/nyregion/sliwa-beret-mayor-republican.html |url-access=registration |access-date=August 8, 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]]}} Additionally, Sliwa started attempting to court [[Labor unions in the United States|labor unions]], portraying himself as pro-worker and anti-[[fat cat]]. As the race entered its final weeks, Sliwa came under increasing pressure from Andrew Cuomo, as well as Republican figures including Trump, to drop out of the race to bolster Cuomo's chances; however, he stated he would rather be executed and [[impaled on a stake]] than drop out and help Cuomo in any way.{{cite web |last1=Fortinsky |first1=Sarah |title=Sliwa: I'd rather be impaled than work for Cuomo |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/5568187-curtis-sliwa-refuses-cuomo-job/ |website=[[The Hill (newspaper)|The Hill]] |access-date=4 November 2025}} Since launching his independent campaign, Cuomo sought to promote a [[centrist]] platform,{{Cite web |last=Kilgore |first=Ed |date=June 25, 2025 |title=June 25: Andrew Cuomo and the New Breed of Self-Styled Combative Centrist |url=https://thedemocraticstrategist.org/2025/06/june-25-andrew-cuomo-and-the-new-breed-of-self-styled-combative-centrist/ |access-date=September 9, 2025 |website=The Democratic Strategist}} stating [[socialism]], specifically the brand Mamdani supports, "has never worked anywhere".{{cite web |last1=Schwartz |first1=Hunter |title=For his rematch with Zohran Mamdani, Andrew Cuomo got a brand-new logo |url=https://www.fastcompany.com/91381224/andrew-cuomo-new-logo-for-zohran-mamdani-rematch |website=[[Fast Company]] |date=August 7, 2025 |access-date=August 8, 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Anuta |first1=Joe |title=Cuomo takes page from Mamdani playbook |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/08/07/cuomo-takes-page-from-mamdani-playbook-00498802 |website=[[Politico]] |date=August 7, 2025 |access-date=August 8, 2025}} Cuomo offered milder alternatives to some of Mamdani's policy platforms such as opposing free busses, arguing they would cost $900 million, instead proposing a $180 million bus subsidy paid for by an increased property tax. On August 6, it was reported by ''The New York Times'' that Cuomo had a phone call with Trump shortly after Trump met with New York Republicans about who they thought was the most likely candidate to potentially beat Mamdani, with a general consensus of a coalescing around a single candidate instead of a four-way split "non-Mamdani" vote.{{cite web |last1=Fandos |first1=Nicholas |last2=Peters |first2=Jeremy W. |last3=Haberman |first3=Maggie |last4=Rosman |first4=Katherine |date=August 6, 2025 |title=Trump Weighs Getting Involved in New York City Mayor Race |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/06/nyregion/trump-nyc-mayor-cuomo-adams-mamdani.html |url-access=registration |access-date=August 8, 2025 |website=[[The New York Times]]}}{{cite web |last1=Dobkin |first1=Rachael |title=Trump calls old foe Andrew Cuomo as he considers intervening in NYC mayor's race to thwart Mamdani: report |url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/world/americas/trump-cuomo-mamdani-nyc-mayor-race-adams-b2803300.html |website=[[The Independent]] |date=August 6, 2025 |access-date=August 8, 2025}} Cuomo's campaign initially issued a statement that the two did not talk about politics on the call, but later backtracked and claimed that the call never happened.{{cite web |last1=Dayak |first1=Shifra |title=Trump Considering Cuomo Support? Cuomo Spox Says Call Between Two Didn't Happen |url=https://www.thecity.nyc/2025/08/06/trump-considering-cuomo-mayor-race/ |website=[[The City (website)|The City]] |date=August 7, 2025 |access-date=August 8, 2025}} Cuomo reportedly said about Trump, "I know, personally, he doesn't want to fight with me. Personally, I don't want to fight with him, right? So I don't think he's going to be eager to create a conflict with us".{{cite news |last1=Fandos |first1=Nicholas |author1-link=Nicholas Fandos |last2=Fitzsimmons |first2=Emma G. |last3=Hirsch |first3=Lauren |date=August 7, 2025 |title=Cuomo Tells Business Leaders He Doesn't 'Personally' Want to Fight Trump |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/07/nyregion/cuomo-trump-mamdani-mayor.html |url-access=registration |archive-url=https://archive.today/20250809071517/https://www.nytimes.com/2025/08/07/nyregion/cuomo-trump-mamdani-mayor.html |archive-date=9 August 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]]}} Trump formally endorsed Cuomo the day before the election alongside [[Elon Musk]]; this was met by dismay from his support base and was described as a "poison pill" and "final nail in the coffin" for his campaign due to just how unpopular both are with New York City Democrats.{{cite web |last1=Stepansky |first1=Joseph |title='Birds of a feather': Trump's endorsement of Cuomo divides NYC voters |url=https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2025/11/4/birds-of-a-feather-trumps-endorsement-of-cuomo-divides-nyc-voters |website=[[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] |access-date=4 November 2025}} The endorsement was also seen as the culmination of weeks of campaigning by Cuomo to eat into Sliwa's voter base in order to close the gap with Mamdani, and was generally well received by the City's Republicans. During his campaign, Mamdani used [[Hindi language|Hindi]] commercials and Indian [[Bollywood]] music to reach his [[South Asian American]] (Desi) voter base.{{cite web |last1=Mukherjee |first1=Renu |title=Desi voters are flexing power — and Zohran Mamdani wooed them hard |url=https://nypost.com/2025/11/04/opinion/desi-voters-are-flexing-power-and-zohran-mamdani-wooed-them-hard/ |access-date=5 |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/etimes/trending/how-zohran-mamdani-used-pop-culture-to-make-politics-personal-for-south-asians-in-new-york/articleshow/122074997.cms |work=[[The Times of |url=https://www.thecentersquare.com/new_york/article_e2a2fcc2-d8ab-4f57-bd7f-e18703dce183.html |website=Center Square |date=August 8, 2025 |access-date=August 8, 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Sheth |first1=Sonam |title=Zohran Mamdani Rips Cuomo After Report That He Spoke With Trump: 'Betrayal' |url=https://www.newsweek.com/zohran-mamdani-andrew-cuomo-trump-betrayal-nyc-2110598 |website=[[Newsweek]] |date=August 7, 2025 |access-date=August 8, 2025}} === Campaign controversies === In July 2025, ''The New York Times'' wrote that on Mamdani's unsuccessful 2009 application to [[Columbia University]], he checked the race boxes "Asian" and "Black or African American". Mamdani confirmed that, but said his intent was to represent his Indian-Ugandan background given the limited options available, and not to improve his chances of admission.{{cite news |last1=Ryan |first1=Benjamin |last2=Fandos |first2=Nicholas |last3=Rubinstein |first3=Dana |date=July 3, 2025 |title=Mamdani Identified as Asian and African American on College Application |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/07/03/nyregion/mamdani-columbia-black-application.html |url-access=registration |access-date=July 4, 2025 |work=[[The New York Times]] |language=en-US |issn=0362-4331 |quote=He was naturalized as a U.S. citizen in 2018 and is now a dual citizen of the United States and Uganda.}} Some of Mamdani's opponents described his action as potentially fraudulent,{{Cite news |last=Stewart |first=Dodai |date=July 5, 2025 |title=Mamdani Once Claimed to Be Asian and African American. He called for unity with Mamdani supporters, saying "we will all help any way we can, because we need our New York City government to work."{{Cite news |last=Glueck |first=Katie |date=2025-11-05 |title=With Trademark Defiance, Cuomo Contemplates Another Loss |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/05/nyregion/cuomo-defeat-mayoral-race.html |access-date=2025-11-05 |work=The New York Times |language=en}} Cuomo did not call Mamdani to concede the election.{{cite news |last=Sommerfeldt |first=Chris |date=5 November 2025 |title=Bitterness marks final moments of mayoral campaign: No Cuomo concession call, Mamdani rails in speech |url=https://www.nydailynews.com/2025/11/05/bitterness-marks-final-moments-of-mayoral-campaign-no-cuomo-concession-call-mamdani-rails-in-speech/ |work=New York Daily News}} Political commentators considered the election loss to be the end of Cuomo's political career.{{Cite web |last=Reisman |first=Nick |date=2025-11-05 |title=He tried to come back from exile. Now Andrew Cuomo's career is over for good. |url=https://www.politico.com/news/2025/11/05/andrew-cuomos-political-career-reaches-an-operatic-conclusion-00637590 |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=Politico |language=en}}{{Cite web |last=Barkan |first=Ross |date=2025-11-05 |title=The End of the Bully |url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/zohran-mamdani-ended-the-politics-of-andrew-cuomo.html |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=Intelligencer |language=en}}{{Cite web |last1=Fischetti |first1=Matthew |last2=Troutman |first2=Matt |date=2025-11-05 |title=Andrew Cuomo lost to Mamdani in NYC Mayoral election lost ends Cuomo family political dynasty |url=https://nypost.com/2025/11/04/us-news/andrew-cuomo-lost-to-mamdani-in-nyc-mayoral-election-lost-ends-cuomo-family-political-dynasty/ |access-date=2025-11-06 |website=[[New York Post]] |language=en-US}} State senator [[Liz Krueger]] said Cuomo never "figured out why he was doing this and what mattered to him," and suggested that he was simply trying to poll better than his father in 1977. Sliwa conceded defeat at 9:24{{nbsp}}pm while addressing voters at an Italian restaurant on the [[Upper West Side]]. Declining to mention Mamdani by name in his concession speech, Sliwa warned the mayor-elect: "If you try to implement socialism, if you try to render our police weak and impotent, if you forsake the people's public safety, we're not only organizing, but we are mobilizing."{{cite web | last=Gold | first=Michael | title=Curtis Sliwa, Back in the Beret, Puts New York's New Mayor on Notice | website=The New York Times | date=2025-11-05 | url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/05/nyregion/curtis-sliwa-concedes.html | access-date=2025-11-05}} Several minutes after conceding defeat, Sliwa called Mamdani to congratulate him on his victory.{{cite news|last=Stieb|first=Matt|title=What Curtis Sliwa Told Zohran Mamdani on Election Night|url=https://nymag.com/intelligencer/article/what-curtis-sliwa-told-zohran-mamdani-on-election-night.html|work=New York Magazine|date=5 November 2025}} Mamdani addressed his supporters around 11:30{{nbsp}}pm. In a celebratory speech that opened with a quote by American socialist [[Eugene V. Debs]], Mamdani repudiated the centrist politics of the Democratic establishment.{{Cite web |last=Stanage |first=Niall |date=5 November 2025 |title=The Memo: Mamdani's triumph ratchets up battle within Democratic Party |url=https://thehill.com/homenews/the-memo/5590204-mamdani-nyc-mayor-win-political-earthquake/ |access-date=6 November 2025 |website=The Hill}} He said of himself and of the Democratic Party:{{Cite news |last1=Rubinstein |first1=Dana |last2=Fahy |first2=Claire |date=2025-11-05 |title=In Mamdani's Victory Speech, He Celebrates a New Political Order |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/05/nyregion/mamdani-speech-victory-nyc.html |access-date=2025-11-06 |work=The New York Times |language=en}} {{blockquote|I am young, despite my best efforts to grow older. I am Muslim. I am a democratic socialist. And most damning of all, I refuse to apologize for any of this. And yet, if tonight teaches us anything, it is that convention has held us back. We have bowed at the altar of caution, and we have paid a mighty price. Too many working people cannot recognize themselves in our party, and too many among us have turned to the right for answers to why they've been left behind. We will leave mediocrity in our past. No longer will we have to open a history book for proof that Democrats can dare to be great.{{Cite news |date=2025-11-05 |title=The full transcript of Zohran Mamdani's victory speech after being elected NYC mayor |url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2025/nov/05/zohran-mamdani-victory-speech-transcript |access-date=2025-11-06 |work=The Guardian |language=en-GB |issn=0261-3077}}}} Mamdani also quoted [[Jawaharlal Nehru]] and invoked the legacy of [[Fiorello La Guardia]].{{cite web |last1=Singh |first1=Anwesha |title=Zohran Mamdani Quotes Jawaharlal Nehru After Winning New York Polls |url=https://www.ndtv.com/world-news/indian-origin-democratic-socialist-zohran-mamdani-quotes-jawaharlal-nehru-after-winning-new-york-polls-9578123 |publisher=[[NDTV]] |access-date=November 5, 2025 |date=November 5, 2025}}{{cite web |last1=Roy |first1=Rajesh |title='Badhai!' In India, a celebration for Zohran Mamdani's New York mayoral win and his roots |url=https://abcnews.go.com/International/wireStory/badhai-india-celebration-zohran-mamdanis-new-york-mayoral-127221396 |publisher=[[ABC News (United States)|ABC News]] |access-date=6 November 2025 |language=en |date=5 November 2025}}{{Cite web |last=Martin |first=Will |date=5 November 2025 |title=A guide to the leaders, revolutionaries, and politicians Zohran Mamdani referenced in his victory speech |url=https://www.businessinsider.com/all-the-thinkers-and-activists-referenced-in-zohran-mamdanis-speech-2025-11 |access-date=6 November 2025 |website=Business Insider}} He said of Cuomo, "let tonight be the final time I utter his name".{{Cite news |last1=Rubinstein |first1=Dana |last2=Fahy |first2=Claire |date=2025-11-05 |title=In a Speech Full of Hope, Mamdani Celebrates a New Political Order |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2025/11/05/nyregion/mamdani-speech-victory-nyc.html |access-date=2025-11-05 |work=The New York Times |language=en}} The ''Times'' called the speech "notably short on conciliatory language". An election for the mayor of New York City was held on November 4, 2025. Democratic state assemblyman Zohran Mamdani won the election with 50.78% of the vote, defeating Republican activist Curtis Sliwa and independent former Democratic governor Andrew Cuomo. This election featured the highest turnout for a New York City mayoral election since 1993, mainly due to significant young voter registration. Mamdani succeeded Democratic incumbent Eric Adams on January 1, 2026, becoming the first Muslim and first South Asian mayor of New York City, as well as its youngest since Hugh J. Grant in 1892.
Adams initially ran for a second term (at first as a Democrat, and later as an independent), but withdrew from the race in September 2025. He remained on the voting ballot because he ended his campaign too late for his name to be removed. Cuomo, pursuing a political comeback after he resigned as New York governor in 2021, was the frontrunner for the Democratic nomination as of early June 2025; however, he was defeated by Mamdani in the Democratic primary in a major upset. Following his primary loss, Cuomo launched an independent campaign. Sliwa, the Republican nominee in the 2021 New York City mayoral election, ran unopposed for his party's nomination.
Mamdani ran on a democratic socialist platform focusing on affordability. Cuomo ran on a broadly centrist platform with a focus on crime and combating antisemitism while also being endorsed by Donald Trump, an endorsement Cuomo declined, while Sliwa criticized both from the political right and advocated tough on crime policies. Mamdani became the first mayoral candidate since 1969 to receive more than one million votes, and the race was the first since 1969 to attract more than two million votes in total.
